_about: Frame configuration for O3 enumeration. Codes, blocks, admission mechanisms and frame types are fixed by the frozen register (sheet 2 of the protocol workbook) and must not be edited here. The `columns` and `tags` blocks are NOT registered: they map this config onto whatever the frozen snapshot files actually look like, and must be confirmed against those files with `python enumerate_o3.py inspect` before the first real run. Every value below marked CONFIRM is a placeholder.
_registered: Frame codes, block, admission_mechanism, frame_type, boundary. Do not change without a preregistration update.
_not_registered: Column names, tag vocabulary, file paths. Change freely to match the snapshots.

_decisions._about: Decisions recorded here are the lead reviewer's, made before any frame was captured, any snapshot taken, or any organization enumerated. They are config choices the registration leaves to execution, not amendments to it.

cfa_location_rule.summary: CFA records with an undeterminable location stay in the frame; C2 decides them at O4. See frames.CFA.boundary.

FORD.name: Ford Foundation grants database (Technology and Society)
FORD._two_source: SINGLE SOURCE as of 2026-09-23. The register defined this as a two-source frame — the live database plus the 990-PF filings from 2011 — because the live database was thought to show only active grants. The capture disproved that: the database reports min_year 2011 and returned 4,319 grants spanning 2011-2026, including long-closed ones. The 990-PF tail is dropped, as a correction to a source justified by a property the frame does not have. NOT claimed: that the filings would have added nothing; that was not measured. Known limitation: the filings may reach back to ~2006 where the database begins at 2011, so roughly five years of depth may be traded; recorded in notes.txt §5 rather than resolved. The source_route column is RETAINED though it now takes one value (live_database_<date>), so the filings can be added later without a schema change.
FORD._route: DEVIATION from the registered route, 2026-09-23. The register says 'manual export of the topic-filtered view'. No topic filter exists: the UI exposes only Approval date and Amount facets, search matches grantee names only, and the program appears solely as a field on each grant. The REST route accepts no program, subject or location parameter either, so filtering at capture was never possible. Captured instead from the rendered HTML documents (payload embedded in div.grants-db), unfiltered, via ford_fetch.py fetch-html with a Turnstile clearance obtained manually in a browser. The narrowing moved from capture time to the boundary below. See notes.txt §1-2.

boundary._decided: DECISION by the lead reviewer, 2026-09-23, before any record was screened or coded. A grant is inside the FORD frame if its program is Technology and Society OR it carries a Technology subject. Approximately 618 grants, collapsing to fewer organizations once grants are deduplicated at O3.
boundary._why: The registered purpose is Ford's technology-and-society grantmaking, not its Technology and Society budget line. Of 400 grants Ford itself tags with a Technology subject, 80 sit in other current programs — 70 of them in Civic Engagement and Government, which is squarely the tradition Block A exists to cover. Those are not a labelling artifact; they are grants Ford tags as technology while funding them from a different program. A program-only boundary would discard them on an internal accounting distinction. A further 42 sit under 'Other Grantmaking', the residual label applied to pre-2018 grants that did not map onto the current structure, and carry the frame's historical depth.
boundary._what_it_admits: Grants whose technology tag is incidental to the organization's work. That is what C3 (constitutive technology) exists to remove — remove the technology and ask whether the core activity survives. The wider boundary hands that judgment to the registered criterion rather than pre-empting it with a program label, which is the same reasoning used for the CTFG country-missing records and the CFA location_rule. Expect heavier C3 attrition in this frame than in an identity frame.
boundary._what_it_costs: A larger screening load, and a frame whose composition depends on Ford's own subject tagging, which the study does not control and cannot audit. Reported as a limitation, not resolved.

_measured._report: Both boundary counts are reported in the write-up as a measured bound on frame completeness — what this frame would have contained under the narrower rule — in the same manner as the CTFG boundary audits. The difference, 280 grants, is the quantity at stake in the choice.

CFA.name: Code for America brigades (archived)
CFA._pin: Pinned to commit 6c5654c7fd9b9f9f236fcf6687d91f422efec050 of github.com/codeforamerica/brigade-information, file organizations.json. Captured 2026-09-23/24; the raw file was archived at its commit URL on 2026-09-24, which matters more here than for ACT because this repository records a program Code for America wound down in June 2023. tags._confirm: STILL UNCONFIRMED as of 2026-09-24 — THIS BLOCKS ENUMERATION OF THIS FRAME. The lists above are guesses taken from the register's prose description, not observations of the file. The reader refuses on an empty include_any but CANNOT tell a wrong tag from a right one, so a mistyped tag yields a silently empty or wrong frame. Run `enumerate_o3.py inspect --frame CFA --file snapshots/CFA/organizations.json`, which prints the full tag inventory with counts, then set include_any, exclude_any and independence_tags from what is actually there and record the inventory in snapshots/CFA/notes.txt §4. The register notes 221 records of which roughly 181 carry a Brigade tag, and that the file also holds 18F, Code for All members, German OK Labs, Code for Poland and government entities.

boundary._decided: DECISION by the lead reviewer, 2026-09-16, before any frame was captured. Records whose location reads US, and records whose location cannot be determined from the roster's city string, stay inside the frame. Only records a location string positively identifies as non-US are dropped at enumeration.
boundary._why: C2 is a human determination made at O4 from the organization's own materials, and it exists precisely because frame location metadata is unreliable. The CTFG boundary already embodies that: it deliberately retains country-missing records rather than letting an absent field decide them. Applying the same logic to CFA keeps the registered division of labour intact — the boundary decides what the frame contains, a person decides whether an organization is US-based — instead of letting a string match at enumeration pre-empt a criterion assigned to a coder.
boundary._what_it_costs: The enumerated count will exceed the register's '~125 US (of 221)' estimate, which assumed a US filter at enumeration. That estimate was written before anyone parsed the city strings and is not a commitment; the count is reported either way and every boundary drop is logged. Each retained UNKNOWN record costs one manual C2 determination at O4, which is small beside the several hundred CTFG records already needing the same treatment.
boundary._what_it_protects: A brigade with a messy or missing city string is likely a small volunteer group with a thin web presence — the tier-2 organizations that do the work without the field vocabulary, which the draw rule goes out of its way to reach before sampling can stop. Dropping them at enumeration would remove them before the stratification that exists to find them.
boundary._alternative_not_taken: keep_us_only would drop undeterminable records too. Still implemented and still switchable, but changing it after enumeration requires re-enumerating, because it changes what the frame contains.

FF.name: Fast Forward portfolio

columns.name: name
columns._location_note: LEFT UNMAPPED DELIBERATELY. The frame's 'Regions' field is the geography the organization's WORK SERVES, not its headquarters: Black Sisters in STEM is US-based and lists Africa, Belgium, Canada, Germany and U.S.; Adalat AI lists Ghana and India. Filtering on it would drop US organizations working abroad and admit foreign organizations working in the US. C2 is determined at O4 from the organization's own materials. 55 of 102 list U.S. as their only region; that is a property of the frame, not a C2 estimate.
columns._from: ffwd_portfolio.csv, produced by ffwd_fetch.py parse. listing_text carries the description, issue areas, regions (labelled BENEFICIARY, not HQ) and technologies.

FF._captured: Captured 2026-09-24 with ffwd_fetch.py v1.0.0 (kept in snapshots/FF/). 102 organizations, matching Fast Forward's own reported total, from 11 pages of https://www.ffwd.org/directory?portfolio=true. See snapshots/FF/notes.txt.
FF._boundary_is_in_the_url: THE ONLY FRAME WHOSE BOUNDARY IS APPLIED AT CAPTURE. Fast Forward publishes two listings from one directory: /directory holds 1,759 organizations that enter by submitting a form, and /directory?portfolio=true holds the 102 accelerator alumni. The register's frame is the portfolio. The difference is not only size: form submission is self-declaration, where this frame's registered admission_mechanism is selection, so capturing the open directory would corrupt a recorded confound rather than merely inflate a count. The fetch script refuses to run if the reported total exceeds 500.

MCGV.name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation grantees
MCGV._unit: The unit in this source is GRANTS, not organizations (register: 795 grants, relationships averaging 3-7 each). The reader deduplicates to organizations within the frame and records grant_count. Some grants route via fiscal sponsors, so the named grantee may be the sponsor.

columns._website_note: RECOVERED SEPARATELY, not in the downloaded CSV. mcgv_urls.py paged the 89 listing pages and joined each grantee's link on by name — all 450 names matched exactly. 334 of 450 grantees have a website in the frame (267 absolute URLs, 67 written as a BARE DOMAIN with no scheme, which a browser resolves relative to the page into a dead mcgovern.org/grants/... link; the domain itself is correct and is read from the source and given a scheme). 116 carry a grantee-website anchor with no href at all and are left BLANK rather than guessed. url_source records which of the three cases each record is, because they are not equally strong evidence. A mcgovern.org URL is never recorded as a grantee's website: at O5 the lexicon proxy would score the funder's vocabulary instead of the grantee's.
columns._location_note: Location is the GRANTEE's own location as the funder records it (Boulder, CO, USA; Nairobi, 110, KEN), not beneficiary geography — closer to C2 than FF's regions field and worth mapping. Still not C2 itself: C2 is determined at O4 from the organization's own materials. No location filter applied at capture.
columns._source_route_note: Single source, so no source_route column. Unlike FORD, which the register defined as two-source.
columns._join: The reader needs website_url on the same rows as the grants. Join mcgv_grantee_urls.csv onto the grants CSV on Grantee before enumerating, or point the reader at a merged file. 450 distinct grantee names across 890 grant rows.

MCGV._captured: CSV downloaded from https://www.mcgovern.org/grants/ on 2026-09-24: 890 grant rows, matching the site's 89 pages at 10 per page. Headers: Grantee, Fiscal Sponsor, Grant, Amount, Focus Area, Location, Date. The register's figure of 795 came from the 990-PF grantee database; the live database covers July 2017 to now and is updated WEEKLY, so it runs ahead of the tax filings. The live database is what the register names.
MCGV._no_filter_applied: Captured unfiltered. The register names no focus-area filter for this frame, unlike FORD. Focus areas include McGovern's legacy brain-research giving — Neuroscience, Legacy, DAF, Matching Gift, N/A — which C3 removes by asking whether the core activity survives without the technology. That judgment belongs to the criterion, not to a capture-time filter.
MCGV._expect: Heavy repetition: MIT, Trek Medics, CarbonPlan, Blue Star Families, Materiom, Upsolve, Jhpiego and Poynter each appear several times in the first two years alone, so 890 grants collapse to far fewer organizations. Heavy fiscal sponsorship: Convergent Research, FFWD, GDI Solutions, Social Good Fund, New Venture Fund, Allied Media Projects, Community Initiatives all appear as sponsors, each firing the Rule 1 clause. Heavy C2 attrition: the most international frame in the register — GBR, KEN, IND, BRA, CHE, ARG, COL, DEU, FRA, ZAF, NGA, ETH, PAK, AUT, CHL, NCL. Some grantees are institutions (MIT, Northeastern, Brown, George Washington, UCSF Foundation), so Rule 1 applies case by case at O3 even though lists_institutions is false for this frame.
MCGV._block_c_overlap: FFWD (Fast Forward) appears here BOTH as a grantee (2024 and 2025, $500,000 each) and as a fiscal sponsor for Materiom and Climate Cabinet Education. The Block C overlap anticipated in snapshots/FF/notes.txt §6 is therefore observed, not predicted. Within block, so it does not enter the multi-frame subset of sensitivity check (f); provenance retained.
